line: Just let me suffer (Just let me breathe) Just let me suffer (Suffer in peace) Just let me suffer (Just let me breathe) Oh, just let me [Breakdown: Oli Sykes & Daryl Palumbo, Daryl Palumbo, Oli Sykes] Just let me suffer Just let me breathe Oh, just let me suffer Suffer in peace
meaning:
Here, Oliver and Daryl could be talking about how religious fanatics ‘force’ their own beliefs on others, how they claim pain, worries, illnesses, syndromes, etc, are because of a “lack of God” in their soul, which can or can’t be true, some do actually relieve their own issues with their faith in God, while others believe that He doesn’t affect them in any way.

They both just want to have their own problems in peace, not having people trying to “solve” them with religion, and not depend on God to be healthy or sane. It’s also worth noting that Oli Sykes is an atheist and has written songs about it.

line: Somebody call the exorcist This is heresy, the child is possessed
meaning:
This is most likely a reference to 1973 horror film “The Exorcist”, which follows a possessed girl and her exorcism by a pair of priests, while her mother tries to rescue her from the entity.
Though initially received with mixed reviews, it is now considered one of the greatest horror films of all time, was the highest-grossing R-rated horror film (before 2017’s It) and commonly considered a classic among horror fans.

Daryl could also be talking about how Christians claims people who criticize Christianity, or religion overall, are ‘possessed’, as if it’s a demon who made them say it, and not the person itself.



A scene from “The Exorcist”, 1973, which the possessed girl floats in air, surprising the priests.

line: Swim the witch, slay the infidel
vault_lines: Swim the witch, slay the infidel
meaning:
During the ninth century in Western Europe, individuals accused of witchcraft or other crimes were subjected to the “swimming test.” According to this method, if the accused person floated on the surface of the water, it was considered proof of guilt and witchcraft, but if they sank to the bottom, they were deemed innocent. This practice gained prominence among Christians who believed that the outcome of the test was a direct divine judgment, with God determining the guilt or innocence of the person on trial.
Credits to Library of Congress Blogs.

line: Get your head from out of my ass
vault_lines: Get your head from out of my ass (Yeah)
meaning:
This is a reference to The Human Centipede film series (2009—2015) directed by Tom Six. In the most popular film of the three, a mad scientist kidnaps and mutilates a trio of tourists in order to reassemble them into a human centipede, created by stitching their mouths to each others' rectums.

In this, Lil Uzi Vert is telling people to leave them alone because all the pressure from people and especially their haters have them feeling like their haters are constantly on their back watching their every move. This could also be a clever way of Lil Uzi Vert telling their haters to “kiss their ass”
